Epsom and Ewell's population increased by around 5,800 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 81,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Epsom and Ewell increased by 7.8%, from just over 75,100 in 2011 to around 80,900 in 2021.

The population here increased at a similar rate to the overall population of the South East (7.5%), but by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Epsom and Ewell was home to around 17.0 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 15.7 in 2011. This area was among the top 30% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was similar in Epsom and Ewell to the South East as a whole

Median age in Epsom and Ewell

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Epsom and Ewell increased by one year, from 40 to 41 years of age.

This area had a similar average (median) age to the South East as a whole in 2021 (41 years) but a slightly higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by around 1,700 (an increase of 12.2%), while the number of residents between 20 and 24 years fell by just over 200 (5.2% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 0.8 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Family in Epsom and Ewell

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children increased in Epsom and Ewell, but fell across the South East.

In Epsom and Ewell, the percentage of households including a couple with dependent children rose from 24.6% in 2011 to 26.1% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 21.0% to 20.6%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Epsom and Ewell fell from 16.9% to 14.9%, while the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children increased from 7.3% to 7.9%.

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children in Epsom and Ewell increased by 1.5 percentage points

Epsom and Ewell stood out from other areas for housing

The percentage of households in the social rented sector increased here, but fell across England.

In Epsom and Ewell, the percentage of households in the social rented sector rose from 8.0% in 2011 to 8.8% in 2021, while across England it fell from 17.7% to 17.1%. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 13.7% to 13.6%.

Private renting in Epsom and Ewell increased from 13.3% to 16.1%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 77.0% to 74.0%.

The rate of social renting in Epsom and Ewell increased by 0.7 percentage points

Unpaid care in Epsom and Ewell

Epsom and Ewell saw the South East's joint largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care (from 7.7% in 2011 to 4.5% in 2021). These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

Every local authority area across the South East saw a fall in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care, as the regional proportion fell from 7.3% to 4.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Epsom and Ewell decreased by 3.2 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Epsom and Ewell

In 2021, 11.4% of Epsom and Ewell residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 8.6% in 2011. The 2.8 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the South East, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 5.2% to 7.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 79.5% of people in Epsom and Ewell identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 85.9% in 2011), while 4.4% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 2.6% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 1.4% in 2011 to 2.8% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 11.4% of usual residents in Epsom and Ewell identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

Religion in Epsom and Ewell

In 2021, 35.7% of Epsom and Ewell residents reported having "No religion", up from 24.3% in 2011. The rise of 11.4 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Epsom and Ewell. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the South East, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.7% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 48.1% of people in Epsom and Ewell described themselves as Christian (down from 61.5%), while 6.1% did not state their religion (down from 7.1% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 35.7% of usual residents in Epsom and Ewell reported having "No religion"

Epsom and Ewell residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 61,600 Epsom and Ewell residents said they were born in England. This represented 76.1% of the local population. The figure has risen from just under 60,700 in 2011, which at the time represented 80.8% of Epsom and Ewell's population.

India was the next most represented, with just over 1,400 Epsom and Ewell residents reporting this country of birth (1.8%). This figure was up from just over 750 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.0% of the population of Epsom and Ewell.

The number of Epsom and Ewell residents born in South Africa rose from around 750 in 2011 (1.0% of the local population) to around 1,200 in 2021 (1.5%).

In 2021, 76.1% of Epsom and Ewell residents reported their country of birth as England

National identity in Epsom and Ewell

In 2021, 10.4% of Epsom and Ewell residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 9.0% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 30 people (3.2%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 1.5% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Epsom and Ewell that identified as "British only" increased from 20.5% to 57.9%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the South East (1.6 percentage points, from 7.1% to 8.7%) than in Epsom and Ewell (1.3 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Epsom and Ewell increased by 1.3 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Epsom and Ewell residents aged 16 years and over, 32.7% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 31.0% in 2011.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater across the South East (2.9 percentage points, from 31.9% to 34.8%) than in Epsom and Ewell (1.7 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Epsom and Ewell increased by 1.7 percentage points

Change in employment

Of Epsom and Ewell residents aged 16 years and over, 60.4% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 60.8% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 40 people (2.3%) said they were unemployed, compared with 2.5% in 2011. The percentage of retired Epsom and Ewell residents decreased from 21.5% to 21.4%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater across the South East (1.3 percentage points, from 59.0% to 57.6%) than in Epsom and Ewell (0.4 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Epsom and Ewell decreased by 0.4 percentage points

Working hours in Epsom and Ewell

In 2021, 10.8% of Epsom and Ewell residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure was at a similar level in 2011 (10.7%).

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week increased from 10.4% to 11.0% across the South East. Across England, the percentage increased from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Epsom and Ewell increased by 0.1 percentage points

Disability in Epsom and Ewell

In 2021, 4.8% of Epsom and Ewell residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 5.9% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion who were identified as being disabled and limited a little remained at 8.3%, while the proportion of Epsom and Ewell residents who were not disabled increased from 85.8% to 86.9%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Epsom and Ewell (1.1 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (1.0 percentage points, from 7.2% to 6.2%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Epsom and Ewell decreased by 1.1 percentage points

Health in Epsom and Ewell

In 2021, 53.2% of Epsom and Ewell residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 50.5% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.6% to 33.3%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Epsom and Ewell residents describing their health as "very bad" was 0.7% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 2.8% to 2.5%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Epsom and Ewell increased by 2.7 percentage points
